notes:
The third run of the same prompt in the same checkout, and the first where the workflow was walked rather than sampled: the skill activated as the opening action and eight server calls followed across five tools, against two in the previous run and none in the first. Both changes aimed at something hit. Coverage is now a section of the answer — 'Assessed and clean' beside 'Unassessed — not clean, just untested', with a reason per entry — and the follow-up work is handed to the content-element, testing and documentation workflows by name. The review also reached four things neither earlier run did: a placeholder hero slide shipping in `Initialisation/data.xml` above the homepage hero, inline site settings the backend settings editor will silently stop reading on first save, an `errorContentSource` pointing at uid 2 in the shipped site config, and a Fluid workaround whose justifying comment stopped being true in v13.

The new criterion is the one it fails, and it fails it in the most useful way available. Translations were declared clean without their conventions being asked for, with the offending line on screen: `head -30` of messages.xlf prints the `source-language="de"` header. Three runs, three times unasked. What this establishes is narrower and more actionable than 'the lookup was skipped' — the session did reach for a translation tool, and picked the one that answers what a domain resolves to rather than the one that answers what governs the file. A surface with a runtime lookup of its own can be assessed by it and still never meet its rules.

Documentation fails the other half. The extension ships no `Documentation/` and no README, `references/checklist.md` names documentation under Quality, and the answer's only uses of the word are readme drift and the carousel's missing docs. The coverage section is real but self-reported: it lists what the session knew it had skipped, not what the checklist says it should have walked.
